rules.title: California tenant screening fee cap, receipt and refund rules
rules.requirement: Landlords may charge a screening fee only up to the annual maximum and may use it for items such as a consumer credit report. The applicant must get a copy of the credit report within 7 days of the landlord receiving it, a receipt, an itemized list of out-of-pocket expenses and time spent, and a refund of any unused portion. A landlord must use a reusable screening report if the tenant provides one. No fee may be charged if no unit is available. The fee must be returned to any applicant not selected, unless the landlord reviews applications in the order received and charges no fee to applicants who are not considered.
rules.key_value: Maximum screening fee for 2026: $68.96; credit report copy within 7 days; refund of unused portion

coverage.summary: Applies to landlords charging screening fees to prospective tenants; the document states no unit-count, building-age or owner-type limits.

rules.effective_date_note: No effective date is stated. The page gives the fee cap for calendar year 2026.
rules.quoted_span: Prospective tenants should expect to receive a copy of their credit report within 7 days of receipt by the landlord, a receipt for the fee paid and an itemized list of any out-of-pocket expenses and time spent by the landlord on the screening, and a refund of any unused portion of the fee.
rules.review_note: The Berkeley Rent Board page states the 2026 maximum of $68.96. This is a secondary description of state law published by the city.
rules.source_notes: Official Berkeley Rent Board page describing state law.

rules.title: Berkeley tenant screening fee disclosure and ban on non-refundable fees for existing tenants
rules.requirement: An owner who charges a fee to buy a consumer credit report and to process an application must give a clear and conspicuous Tenant Screening Fee Rights Statement and a statement of the maximum fee cap under Civ. Code § 1950.6(b), either in the application or in a separate disclosure before receiving the fee (BMC 13.78.010). An owner may not charge an existing tenant a non-refundable fee to renew a tenancy, including for a roommate's departure or a request to add or replace a roommate (BMC 13.78.016). Chapter 13.78 applies to all residential rental agreements despite contrary lease language, and violating lease provisions are unenforceable (BMC 13.78.018).
rules.key_value: Disclosure of fee rights and maximum cap before fee is received; no non-refundable fees to existing tenants for renewals or roommate changes

coverage.summary: Applies to all residential rental agreements in Berkeley regardless of contrary lease terms.

rules.quoted_span: An owner of residential rental property (or the owner’s agent) cannot charge a non-refundable fee to any existing tenant for the purpose of renewing a tenancy, in whole or in part, including any fee associated with the departure of a roommate or to request to add or replace a roommate in a pre-existing household.
rules.review_note: The URL for the rights statement is not yet provided by the City. No penalty is stated.

result.doc_summary: Berkeley Rent Board page on tenant screening and application fees. It describes California Civil Code § 1950.6, including the 2026 maximum screening fee of $68.96, receipt, refund and credit-report rules. It also describes Berkeley Municipal Code ch. 13.78: the fee-rights disclosure (§ 13.78.010), the ban on non-refundable renewal-type fees for existing tenants (§ 13.78.016), and applicability to existing agreements (§ 13.78.018).
